import BanditRLProof.OnlineStrongConvexSourceSubgradient

noncomputable section
open Set
namespace BanditRL.OnlineConvex

theorem stronglyConvex_iff_sourceSubgradient_growth {E : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (d : ℕ) (e : E ≃ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (f : E → EReal) (V : Set E) (lam : ℝ)
    (hf : SourceProper f) (hV : Convex ℝ V) (hlam : 0 ≤ lam)
    (hsub : ∀ p ∈ V,
      (SourceSubdifferential (fun u => f (e.symm u)) (e p)).Nonempty) :
    (∀ x ∈ V, ∀ y ∈ V, ∀ a : ℝ, 0 < a → a < 1 →
      f (a • x + (1 - a) • y) ≤
        (a : EReal) * f x + ((1 - a : ℝ) : EReal) * f y -
          (((lam / 2) * a * (1 - a) * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2 : ℝ) : EReal)) ↔
    (∀ p ∈ V, ∀ q ∈ V, ∀ g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      g ∈ SourceSubdifferential (fun u => f (e.symm u)) (e p) →
        (f p).toReal + inner ℝ g (e (q - p)) +
          (lam / 2) * ‖q - p‖ ^ 2 ≤ (f q).toReal)

end BanditRL.OnlineConvex

Definition4.1 properness inherited by the strong-convexity predicate: forall x, f x != bottom; exists x and real r with f x=coe r. The global witness is used to exclude top at supported points, including after coordinate transport.
Printed convex set V. For x,y in V and nonnegative weights summing to one, their weighted sum belongs to V. Empty V allowed.
Printed lambda >=0; zero allowed, no division by lambda.

Exact printed V subset dom partial f: for every p in V there exists an actual vector g whose GLOBAL coordinate support inequality holds at every u in R^d. No support construction is concluded; no restriction of support evaluation to V.
Universal feasible endpoints, strict 0<a<1. Original E norm and coefficient lambda/2*a*(1-a). Finite values follow internally; endpoint weights need not be added to the source statement.
Universal p,q in V and EVERY global coordinate subgradient at p, not merely a chosen support. Pairing uses e(q-p); quadratic penalty uses original norm(q-p).

same support used for both converse endpoint inequalities

source_delta: This is the full Lemma4.2 iff under its printed V subset dom partial f premise, represented by explicit algebraic coordinates. Properness comes from Definition4.1; it means no bottom anywhere and a genuine finite real witness somewhere. The all-point support premise is supplied, not proved by this theorem. No separate V subset effectiveDomain premise is added: derive it using subgradient_point_finite after transporting properness through e inverse. No isometry or Euclidean penalty substitution is allowed. This is finite-dimensional coordinate representation, not an infinite-dimensional iff claim. Empty V, lambda0 and d0 are allowed by the core statement. Closedness, global convexity of f and minimizer attainment are not assumed.
source_proof_correction: Printed35/PDF47 has an erroneous second equality in the converse proof. The valid chain is 0=the weighted pairing <= a*f(x)+(1-a)*f(y)-f(z)-(lambda/2)a(1-a)||x-y||^2. The iff statement is unchanged; no saturation/equality assumption is added. The strict residual1/2 in the concrete canary refutes that printed equality and validates the inequality correction.
implementation_spine: Transport the actual properness witness to coordinates. At each feasible p choose a support from the explicit all-point premise and apply subgradient_point_finite to derive f(p)<top; combine with no-bottom to obtain the finite-value identity. The forward implication genuinely calls stronglyConvex_sourceSubgradient_growth on the original f,V,lambda,e and the internally derived domain inclusion. For the converse put z=a*x+(1-a)*y in V and choose ONE actual global support g at z. Apply the hypothesized quadratic growth to (z,x) and (z,y), multiply by a and1-a, and add. The weighted pairing cancels. Original norm homogeneity gives ||x-z||^2=(1-a)^2||x-y||^2 and ||y-z||^2=a^2||x-y||^2, yielding exactly the source curvature term. Finally convert finite real values back to EReal. The source forward proof instead uses support based at y evaluated at a*x+(1-a)*y, division by positive a and the limit a down to0; implementation reuse and source topology are kept distinct.
consumers: The first closed experimental consumer uses E=R^2 with the sup norm, e=2 times ordinary coordinates, V=[-1,1]^2, and globally finite f(x)=(x0^2+x1^2)/2+x0. For every p it explicitly produces the global covector (p+(1,0))/2. It characterizes every global support algebraically and proves the quadratic growth premise independently, then its first conjunction genuinely applies the iff CONVERSE to obtain interpolation. At q=(1,1), original squared norm1 differs from coordinate squared norm8; pairing1 and f(q)=2 refute a substituted coordinate penalty5<=2. The same example at x=q,y=-q,a=1/2 has weighted residual1/2, so equality to0 is false. The second consumer proves f(t)=-t^2 proper with an EMPTY global subdifferential at every point. Support-indexed lambda0 growth is vacuous, but midpoint interpolation would require0<=-1. This is a counterexample to removing the all-point support premise, not to Lemma4.2. The concrete quadratic is globally finite; the canaries do not test top outside V, empty V, d0 or exhaustive edge coverage.
